drafted_by: Claude (from the abstracts of the 25 papers)

questions.question: Which papers aim to make question answering explainable, faithful or attributable, and how?
questions.reference_answer: Entailment trees built with Monte-Carlo planning (FAME); rationales learned without supervision (Hop, Union, Generate); evidential paths for knowledge graph reasoning (SQUIRE); interpretable logic rules (deep inductive logic reasoning); attributing answers to retrieved sources (cross-lingual attribution).

evidence.quote: The reasoning steps are organized as a structured entailment tree
not only predicts answers but also identifies rationales
provide interpretable predictions on missing links with evidential paths
logic-based approaches provide interpretable rules to infer the target answer
attribute the answer to a retrieved source

questions.question: What role do data augmentation, counterfactuals or simulated data play in the corpus?
questions.reference_answer: Hidden space augmentation of training samples (QADA); counterfactual training and evaluation data created by retrieve-generate-filter; user feedback simulated from supervised data (bandit learning).

evidence.quote: introduces a novel data augmentation pipeline used to augment training QA samples
create counterfactual evaluation and training data with minimal human supervision
simulating feedback using supervised data

questions.question: How do the papers deal with long documents or evidence spread over several documents?
questions.reference_answer: Long context documents with logically related information (ConditionalQA); a global memory over a long document (GEMFormer); questions that need reasoning across multiple documents (WikiHowQA).

evidence.quote: long context documents with information that is related in logically complex ways
This task includes processing a long document and reasoning over the multiple parts of it
many questions require reasoning across multiple documents

questions.question: Which papers study long-form or non-factoid answers, and what problems do they point out?
questions.reference_answer: Experts judge long-form answers and no existing metric predicts their preferences (critical evaluation of LFQA); non-factoid answers are passage-level and hard to construct and evaluate (WikiHowQA); longer candidate answers make matching with gold answers harder (evaluating open-domain QA with LLMs).

evidence.quote: no existing metrics are predictive of human preference judgments
requiring passage-level answers that are difficult to construct and evaluate
candidate answers become longer

questions.question: Which papers build their method around a pre-trained language model or an encoder-decoder Transformer, and for what?
questions.reference_answer: An encoder-decoder Transformer translating a query into a path (SQUIRE) and acting as a knowledge graph embedding model (sequence-to-sequence KG completion and QA); a pre-trained language model that supports subgraph reasoning (ReasoningLM); retriever and reranker as attention inside one Transformer (You Only Need One Model); a pre-trained language model aligning questions and KG artifacts (ALCQA).

evidence.quote: utilizes an encoder-decoder Transformer structure to translate the query to a path
an off-the-shelf encoder-decoder Transformer model can serve as a scalable and versatile KGE model
develop a more capable PLM that can directly support subgraph reasoning for KGQA
within the transformer architecture
utilize a pretrained language model to implicitly align the question and KG artifacts

questions.question: Which papers handle special kinds of questions, such as temporal, numeric or conditional ones?
questions.reference_answer: Temporal questions over knowledge graphs (SF-TQA); multi-step quantitative reasoning where numeric and verbal cues interact (compositional generalization); answers that only hold under certain conditions (ConditionalQA).

evidence.quote: Answering factual questions with temporal intent over knowledge graphs
Quantitative reasoning is an important aspect of question answering
the answers are only applicable when certain conditions apply

questions.question: Which papers improve the retriever-reader pipeline of open-domain question answering, and how?
questions.reference_answer: A knowledge graph linking the retrieved passages (KG-FiD); merging retriever, reranker and reader into one model (You Only Need One Model); a verbalizer that turns structured data into text for the retriever and reader (unified knowledge interface).

evidence.quote: uses a knowledge graph to establish the structural relationship among the retrieved passages
a single question answering model trained end-to-end
retrieverreader framework

questions.question: Which papers rewrite or transform questions, text or data as a step in their method?
questions.reference_answer: Rewriting questions to align them with actions (ALCQA); rewriting snippets so that they can be read on their own (decontextualization); turning structured data into text (data-to-text verbalizer).

evidence.quote: We train a question rewriting model to align the question and each action
rewrite snippets from scientific documents to be read on their own
use the data-to-text method as a means for encoding structured knowledge

questions.question: Which papers point out weaknesses of existing models, metrics or practices, and which weaknesses?
questions.reference_answer: Metrics do not predict expert preferences (LFQA evaluation); lexical matching fails when a plausible answer is not in the gold list (evaluating open-domain QA); models rely on shortcuts instead of multi-hop reasoning (counterfactual multihop QA); raw generations of generative models often fall short in factuality (attribution for cross-lingual QA).

evidence.quote: no existing metrics are predictive of human preference judgments
lexical matching fails completely when a plausible candidate answer does not appear in the list of gold answers
the existing QA models always rely on shortcuts
their raw generations often fall short in factuality

questions.question: Which papers propose one unified or simplified model in place of a multi-stage pipeline?
questions.reference_answer: One model for retrieval, reranking and reading (You Only Need One Model); one encoder-decoder Transformer in place of a multi-stage KGE pipeline (sequence-to-sequence KG completion and QA); a single PLM instead of PLM plus GNN (ReasoningLM); one unified model for many tasks (long-tailed QA).

evidence.quote: This allows us to use a single question answering model trained end-to-end
integrated into a multi stage pipeline
we aim to simplify the above two-module approach
building a unified QA model supporting various tasks is vital
